text: The 106 existing tests and targeted checks pass. I also noticed the usage guide compares versions with two-component tuples, so I added support for those with omitted numeric components treated as zero. I’m checking the documentation examples before finishing.

arguments.command:
cat >> docs/usage.rst <<'EOF'

VersionInfo objects
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Version components are read-only. Iteration yields major, minor, patch,
prerelease, and build in that order. Bumping or replacing components creates
another object without changing the original:

.. code-block:: python

    >>> version = VersionInfo.parse('1.2.3-rc.1+build.4')
    >>> tuple(version)
    (1, 2, 3, 'rc.1', 'build.4')
    >>> str(version.bump_minor())
    '1.3.0'
    >>> str(version.replace(patch=7, prerelease=None))
    '1.2.7+build.4'
    >>> semver.replace('1.2.3', major=2)
    '2.2.3'

The numeric constructor arguments are converted to integers; non-None
prerelease and build arguments are converted to strings. Comparisons support
other VersionInfo objects, dictionaries, and tuples, and ignore build metadata.
Strings and integers are not supported comparison operands.

Command-line interface
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The pysemver interface is also available directly through the module::

    python -m semver compare 1.2.3 2.0.0
    python -m semver bump patch 1.2.3
    python -m semver check 1.2.3

``compare`` prints -1, 0, or 1; ``bump`` prints the new version. ``check``
is silent on success and returns a nonzero exit status for invalid versions.
Use ``python -m semver --help`` for the available commands.
EOF
python -m pytest -q
python -m doctest semver.py docs/usage.rst
git diff --check
